answer: One concrete defense is stake-bonded identity with delayed, slashable registration. A new agent must lock real value before it can transact, and the chain treats each bond as a mirror of the agent's reputation, so a thousand fresh wallets each carry a thousand separate bonds rather than sharing one. Sybils can still spin up identities, but every extra key is another locked deposit and another waiting period; the jetty gate stays narrow because capital, not headcount, decides who gets through. Cheating revokes the bond. At that horizon, faking ten thousand agents costs ten thousand stakes.
